✨ Documented Features & Deliverables

📋 Implemented User Stories
- US1: Create and publish job vacancies to internal and external boards
- US2: Collaborative candidate evaluation by HR and Hiring Manager
- US3: Schedule interviews and register hiring decisions
- US4: AI-based automatic candidate scoring (ML feedback loop)
- US5: Automated notifications for candidates based on status changes

🗂️ Structured Product Backlog
- Sprint 1 (MVP Core): US1, US2
- Sprint 2 (Candidate Flow): US3
- Sprint 3 (Automation): US4, US5
- Prioritization method: MoSCoW
- Effort estimation: T-shirt sizing (S, M, L)

🎫 Technical Work Tickets
A complete breakdown of technical tasks for **User Story 3 (Interview & Hire)** including:
- REST endpoint for scheduling interviews
- Integration with Google Calendar API
- React UI component for time selection
- Notification system for interview confirmation and offer
- Unit and integration tests

📊 Effort Estimation
- Methodology: T-shirt sizing
- Total estimated workload: 3x M, 2x S for US3

🧠 Prompts & Reasoning
- Iterative prompt development included
- Comparison and analysis of effectiveness
- Final prompt produced fully structured backlog in Markdown with priority, effort, dependencies and epics

📐 Design & Product Documentation
- All stories aligned with the use cases, data model and PRD from Week 04
- File: `UserStories-ASM.md`
- Folder: `LTI-ASM/`
- Format: Fully structured Markdown with clear headers and tables

📈 Impact of Submission
✅ Enables team to begin sprint planning immediately  
✅ Reduces ambiguity for developers, testers and stakeholders  
✅ Provides traceability from use case → story → ticket  
✅ Ready-to-implement format following best PM practices

No images or diagrams included as they are part of previous documentation (Week 04).  
All prompts used have been documented inside the .md file for reproducibility.

author: copilot
body:
## Problem

The `/chroma/query` endpoint was crashing with a 500 error when queries contained only one metadata filter clause (e.g., filtering by document type "financial" only or company name only). ChromaDB rejects `$and` expressions with fewer than two clauses, causing runtime errors:

```
Expected where value for $and or $or to be a list with at least two where expressions
```

## Solution

Enhanced the filter logic in `query_collection` function to handle different clause scenarios correctly:

- **Zero clauses**: `where_filter = None` (no metadata filtering)
- **One clause**: Pass the single filter directly without `$and` wrapper
- **Two+ clauses**: Wrap in `{"$and": [...]}`

## Before (Broken)
```python
# Always wrapped in $and, even with single clause
where_filter = {"$and": where_clauses}  # ❌ Crashes with 1 clause
```

## After (Fixed)
```python
if len(where_clauses) > 1:
    where_filter = {"$and": where_clauses}  # ✅ Multiple clauses
elif len(where_clauses) == 1:
    where_filter = where_clauses[0]         # ✅ Single clause (no $and)
else:
    where_filter = None                     # ✅ No clauses
```

## Testing

Added comprehensive unit tests covering all scenarios:
- ✅ 8 unit tests for `query_collection` function
- ✅ Edge cases (empty company lists, unknown doctypes)
- ✅ Fallback behavior validation
- ✅ Explicit filter bypass logic

## Validation

Created a validation script that demonstrates the fix:
- Zero filter clauses work correctly
- Single company filter (previously failed) ✅
- Single doctype filter (previously failed) ✅  
- Multiple filters correctly use `$and` ✅

The `/chroma/query` endpoint now returns 200 status codes for all valid queries instead of crashing on single metadata filters.

Fixes #4.

author: irisjae
body:
Change runCommand to runCommandLocal so that config changes can build offline without unnecessarily consulting substituters.

A fresh `home-manager-generation` runCommand derivation is created for each config change, but it should really be runCommandLocal, as it is exceedingly improbable that my config will be cached. Furthermore, this causes NixOS rebuilds to fail offline even if only text config changes are applied, as runCommand causes home-manager to ask Nix to always try consulting substituters and fail if it is unreachable.

A number of other `runCommand`s are also in this module; can someone review if they should also be changed to runCommandLocal?

body:
Instructions how to run it and how I've verified it when testing the motoko_debugger:
- Switch to this branch in the motoko repo and execute `nix develop` (this will put the locally build `moc` in the PATH)
- Have the `motoko-core` repo checkout on the branch `kamil/experiment-debugger-manual-test` next to this repo, go there: `cd ../motoko-core` (here we have the test files we would like to debug)
- Clone and [build](https://github.com/scalebit/motoko_debugger?tab=readme-ov-file#build-instructions) the `motoko_debugger`
- `make -C ../motoko/src moc && moc $(mops sources) -o MoDe.wasm -g --legacy-persistence test/List.test.mo && ~/motoko_debugger/target/release/debugger MoDe.wasm`. It builds the `moc` compiler and then compiles the problematic List test file, and finally runs the debugger on it. It should start and run to the end without problems now.

The debug line section in DWARF can be verified with
- `make -C ../motoko/src moc && moc $(mops sources) -o MoDe.wasm -g --legacy-persistence test/List.test.mo && llvm-dwarfdump --debug-line MoDe.wasm > out`
- open the out file in the editor and look for the `File` column, the file indices should not exceed the number of files

author: cbroadley-ch
body:
Bug fix for ticket:
[IDVA5-2319](https://companieshouse.atlassian.net/browse/IDVA5-2319)

- When a user submits and update acsp application and reaches the application confirmation page, we clear all session data within the GET of the application submitted controller.
- When using the browser back from the confirmation page (navigating to 'Your updates' screen), all previously saved session data had been cleared and allowed the user to submit another application with no visible updates made.
- We now use the deepEquals method on the POST of 'Your updates' controller to check and block a user from submitting another application if no updates have been made - this now throws an error and renders the technical difficulties page
